action: KPMG Canada clients: expect direct contact from KPMG, ask what tax documents were involved, and watch for tax-themed phishing and CRA account misuse.
date_note: Date KPMG confirmed the incident; the date of the intrusion was not stated.
exec: A major professional-services firm says an outside party reached clients' tax files. Check what you shared with advisers and who holds it.
plain: KPMG Canada says someone outside the firm got into some clients' tax documents. It has not said how many clients or files, or how the intruder got in.

sources.name: The Globe and Mail report via 102.7 WBOW

summary: KPMG Canada confirmed on 18 November that an outside party gained unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents. The Globe and Mail reported it first. KPMG says it has secured its systems and is contacting affected clients, and that its monitoring shows the information is not online or being misused. It has not said how many clients or files were affected or how the access happened.
title: KPMG Canada confirms unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents

validation.note: KPMG's statement as relayed by Reuters and in coverage of the Globe and Mail's first report; both read are secondary relays of the same statement. KPMG's own notice and the Globe article were not read.

review.note: Compared with Reuters relays: 18 Nov, secured systems, contacting clients, not online or misused, no numbers disclosed
